title: /weather <location> answers 'saved as an idea' instead of the forecast

rootCause.summary: The explicit /weather shortcut routes to the weather_query scenario, which depends on the LLM emitting a weather_lookup tool call (direct_output_from_tool short-circuits only AFTER the call). The configured local model (qwen3:30b) sometimes returns no tool call and no final (llm_returned_no_tool_calls_and_no_final), producing OutcomeProviderError. Because weather_query is requires_provenance and the assembler yields empty Sources, the provenance gate rewrites the provider-error into the capture-as-fallback body 'saved as an idea — i'll surface it later.' Geocoding was never the cause (Open-Meteo resolves the ZIP directly).

resolution: Add a deterministic /weather fast-path (facade Step 3.9) that dispatches the weather tool directly for an explicit /weather <location> shortcut, bypassing the LLM loop AND the provenance gate. Extract weather.LookupForecast (shared core of the tool handler) and wire it as a facade seam (WithWeatherLookup). Success renders forecast_line + one SourceExternalProvider; provider failure / empty location render an honest StatusUnavailable/slot_missing line — NEVER the capture-as-fallback acknowledgement. Backward-compatible: the LLM /weather path is untouched when the seam is not wired. Three adversarial unit tests reproduce the pre-fix provider-error and assert the fast-path bypasses it; regression-quality-guard --bugfix PASS.
codeVsDeployment: deployed. The fix (sourceSha d4755abd, incl. the grpc v1.82.1 CVE bump) is built, operator-cosign-signed, deployed, and running on <deploy-host>. Running container digests match the fix build (core sha256:44ed9984, ml sha256:30ea2392), both healthy, and the Telegram assistant adapter is wired and bound. Only the operator's behavioral Telegram smoke test remains (an authenticated HTTP probe returned 401 because prod requires a PASETO session, not the raw shared token).

All four requested domains came back CLEAN. Goroutine/lifecycle: a whole-file scan of facade.go for `go func`/`go ident(`/time.After/time.NewTicker/time.NewTimer returns ZERO matches, so no goroutine or timer can leak per turn; handleWeatherShortcut is straight-line, holds no lock and registers no cleanup; the path returns before Step 4 so it starts NO span, and zero started is trivially zero leaked. Concurrency: the premise is real (one goroutine per HTTP request into one shared *Facade, and wireAssistantFacade runs in a background goroutine while the listener already accepts POST /api/assistant/turn per cmd/core/main.go:541,564), and the seam is nonetheless safe on four counts — weatherLookup is write-once (sole write facade.go:335, sole caller wiring:241, all 7 references enumerated); the wired closure captures nothing mutable (package-level LookupForecast + the constant WindowNow); the plain write is PUBLISHED through a synchronizing operation because it is sequenced before SetAdapter at wiring:409, which is h.adapter.Store over atomic.Pointer[HTTPAdapter] (late_binding.go:33,42) whose matching Load in ServeHTTP establishes happens-before, with LateBoundHandler fail-closed at 503 before that store; and the state behind the seam is already guarded (services by servicesMu sync.RWMutex, the LRU by mu sync.Mutex across Get/Put/Len). Resource usage: bounded at ~4s per cold-cache turn by http.Client{Timeout: 2s} over two sequential round trips, with NO retry construct in the package and a 128-entry TTL cache; the client timeout spans the body read, so the unbounded-looking json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode cannot be held open. The tool's PerCallTimeoutMs: 8000 does NOT apply to the fast path (it belongs to the bypassed tool-call loop) and does not need to — the 2s transport bound is strictly tighter and governs both paths. Config/deployment: a disabled or misconfigured skill yields weather_tools_not_configured, rendered as StatusUnavailable + provider_unavailable + an honest 'couldn't get the weather' line and NEVER StatusSavedAsIdea, so the masking this bug removed stays removed on the config-failure branch too. Cause-token conflation between permanent misconfiguration and transient outage was checked before being written up and is FORCED by the 8-member closed vocabulary in contracts/response.go:194-229 (no config-missing token exists; internal_error would be actively wrong), so it was deliberately NOT recorded as a finding. completedPhaseClaims.summary: Security review of the ONE new data path 2f35e26f introduces: a user-controlled location string reaching an outbound third-party HTTP call, and provider-controlled data reaching a user-visible chat body. Five axes, all CLEAN for this packet's changed surface. INPUT: the location is never concatenated into a URL — both requests build their query through net/url (open_meteo.go:223-227 geocode, :290-300 forecast) and q.Encode() percent-encodes the value, closing parameter injection and CR/LF request-splitting (net/http's own control-character rejection is a second independent barrier). SSRF is structurally impossible: the user contributes only the VALUE of the `name` parameter; scheme/host/path come from p.geocodeURL / p.forecastURL, injected from SST and fail-loud (NewOpenMeteoProvider PANICS on an empty endpoint, open_meteo.go:113-125), with no user-reachable seam that rewrites the host. OUTPUT: provider-controlled forecast_line and provider_name reach the body and Sources, but the Telegram renderer escapes on every body-carrying branch (escapeForMode at render_outbound.go:166 sourced-answer, :198 default, :243 footer) BEFORE ParseMode is set at :73, and escapeMarkdownV2 covers the full closed Telegram set (:320-355); the deployed mode is markdown_mode: "MarkdownV2" (config/smackerel.yaml:1312). The reflected user location never reaches the Telegram wire at all — StatusUnavailable routes to renderError, which emits the single-line "<skill>: <cause>" form and drops resp.Body (:175-180, :300-312). SECRETS: grep for api_key|token|secret|password|credential|auth across the whole non-test weather package returns NO output — the provider is key-less by design (open_meteo.go:9-11) and no Authorization header is set on either request. The credential-in-URL error risk named in the brief is closed by construction: handleWeatherShortcut binds err and then DISCARDS it, substituting a fixed sentence (facade.go:1402-1407), so no upstream error string, URL, query string or header echo can reach the user, the audit record or a log line; the fast path emits no span and no log of its own, so there is no third sink. AUTHZ: enumerating the Handle step markers settles the bypass question by ORDERING — handlePendingConfirm runs at :634, resolvePendingDisambig at :674, the clarification gate at :879 and the side-effect confirmation gate at :926/:936, ALL upstream of Step 3.9 at :993, so the fast path cannot bypass any of them; a confirm reply is consumed at Step 1 and 3.9 fires only on a literal /weather prefix, which is not a confirm reply and executes no pending action. The fast path still calls appendTurnAndPersist and writeAudit (facade.go:1007-1008), so per-user persistence and audit are NOT skipped. A non-test grep for ratelimit|rate_limit|limiter|quota|throttle across internal/assistant returns NO matches — the facade has no limiter on ANY path, so there is no differential to bypass. What 3.9 genuinely skips (LLM loop, router/borderline band, capture-as-fallback gate) is routing machinery, not security control; skipping the capture gate IS the fix. DOS: the geocode retry list is capped at TWO entries by construction (strings.Index finds the FIRST comma only and appends at most one extra attempt, open_meteo.go:198-210), so a thousand-comma location still yields 2 geocode attempts — worst case is <=3 upstream requests per turn (an honest refinement of the brief's 'two round trips'), a constant that cannot grow with input length; responses decode into fixed structs and the body is budget-truncated by the transport. MECHANICAL FLOOR: security-gate.sh exit 1, 12 inline-credentials findings, ALL in scripts/commands/config.sh and scripts/commands/config_secret_rejection_test.sh — files this packet's fix commit never touched. Reported and attributed at repo level, not suppressed, no exemption added, and NOT re-run with a narrowed scope to manufacture a 0.
